summary: Choose which cloud providers to install. Backblaze B2 and OneDrive now download separately and have their own release histories.

items.text: Open Connectors to install Backblaze B2 for backup and sync or OneDrive for file transfers. A transfer between the two can install both required packs in one review.
Review each pack's publisher, source, capabilities and dependencies before installing. Import a private signed connector or build one using the .NET connector SDK and starter project.
Settings shows app and connector updates separately. Choose automatic connector updates, review new dependencies and roll back an installed pack to its previous version.

Jobs that need a missing pack pause with their checkpoints intact. Accounts and folder mappings survive connector removal, and saved sync roots protect an in-use provider from removal or disabling. The app offers a compatible pack when its catalog also lists a newer SDK requirement.

Each provider has its own GitHub release history. A shared signed catalog authenticates downloads, including the original 1.0.0 packages and their publisher. The EXE, MSI, ZIP and Store MSIX all start with the same provider-free host.

installationNotes: After updating from 1.2.2, open Connectors and install the providers your saved accounts, transfers or backup folders use. An internet connection is required to download an official pack.
Connectors run with your Windows user permissions. Review the publisher before installing an official or private pack. Microsoft Store installations receive app updates through the Store.

items: The merged app built with zero warnings or errors and passed all 1,662 non-live Release tests, including startup recovery and connector behavior. Release automation passed 141 assertions.

An isolated profile downloaded both existing public 1.0.0 packs and verified installation, loading, disabling, re-enabling and removal for each. Cross-provider transfer checks use simulated provider endpoints.

storeStatus: The GitHub MSIX is the unsigned package prepared for Microsoft Store submission. Microsoft controls certification and rollout of the Store update.
